I am an old woman, sixty years now, and I have farmed beans on this land for many seasons. Beans do not need the white fertilizer like maize does — the plant feeds itself from the soil. But the insects, ah, the insects will eat everything if I do nothing, so I must buy some powder for spraying when the pods come. I keep my seeds from last harvest as my mother taught me, and my children and grandchildren will help with the weeding, though I may call one or two young men for the clearing at the start.
